title: Tallowmere TK75 Review After 3 Weeks: Good Budget Hot-Swap Keyboard?
description: My honest thoughts on the Tallowmere TK75 after three weeks of daily use: build, switches, sound, software and battery. Unit provided by the manufacturer; no payment and no review approval.

content.authorization_basis: Original synthetic transcript authored for the AI Video Discovery project. No real video exists.

segments.text: Alright, so this is the Tallowmere TK75.
I've been using it for about three weeks as my main keyboard,
and I want to give you my honest thoughts.
Quick disclaimer, they sent me this unit for free,
but they haven't seen this video and they're not paying me for it.
So, first impressions. The box is fine, nothing special.
You get the keyboard, a braided cable, a keycap puller and a switch puller, which tells you it's hot-swappable.
That means you can pull the switches out and put different ones in without soldering.
If you're new to this, that's actually a pretty big deal,
because it lets you experiment with different switches without buying a whole new board.
The layout is seventy-five percent.
So you lose the number pad and some of the keys on the right,
but you keep the function row and the arrow keys. For me that's the sweet spot.
I used to have a full-size board and honestly I never touched the number pad.
Your mileage may vary if you do a lot of spreadsheets. Build quality.
The case is plastic.
It's not bad plastic, but if you press in the middle, there's a little bit of flex.
Not a dealbreaker at this price, but you'll notice it.
The switches it ships with are linear, which means there's no bump and no click,
it just goes straight down. They're pretty smooth out of the box.
I'd say a bit scratchy on a few keys, and the space bar especially had a rattle at first.
I actually went down a rabbit hole about stabilizers for like two days.
Anyway, I ended up putting a little bit of lube on it and it's mostly fine now.
Sound. People care a lot about the sound.
Let me type a bit so you can hear it.
So it's kind of a muted thock, I'd call it. There's some foam inside, which helps.
It's not the deepest-sounding board I've tried, but it doesn't sound hollow either.
Software. This is the weak point.
The software to remap keys only works on one operating system, and it crashed on me twice.
You can do some remapping with function key shortcuts on the board itself,
but the manual explaining them is pretty confusing. Battery.
It has a wireless dongle and Bluetooth, and they say around two hundred hours with the backlight off.
I haven't had it die on me yet.
I charge it maybe once every week and a half with the lights on low.
So, would I recommend it?
If you're getting into mechanical keyboards and you want something hot-swappable without spending a lot, yeah,
I think it's a solid pick.
If you're picky about software, or you want a heavy aluminum case, look elsewhere.
Let me know what keyboard you're using right now in the comments, I'm always curious. Thanks for watching.
